title: Darmstadt
description: A former ducal capital south of Frankfurt with one of the strongest technical universities in Germany and a large research and IT industry.
html:
Science city with a courtly past

Darmstadt sits half an hour south of Frankfurt and calls itself a city of science, a title it earned: the European Space Operations Centre, a heavy-ion research institute and a cluster of software companies are based here, and the technical university is one of the country's leading engineering schools. The Art Nouveau colony on the Mathildenhöhe, a UNESCO site, reminds visitors that the city was once the seat of a grand duke with a taste for the arts.

Studying and working here

Around 40,000 students at three institutions give the city of 160,000 a young feel. The technical university offers strong programmes in mechanical and electrical engineering, computer science and materials science, many with English-taught master's tracks. The job market is unusually good for graduates: IT, aerospace, chemicals and pharmaceuticals are all within commuting distance, and Frankfurt's financial sector is a short train ride away. Rents are lower than in Frankfurt but rising; apply for student housing early.
